routes.title: 🏙️ Understand a 3D scene
routes.summary: Point features → semantic labels → object instances
routes.goal: Connect point-cloud representations to the objects and regions a scene contains.

steps.label: Learn point representations
steps.focus: Compare whole-set features with hierarchical local geometry.

steps.label: Compare scalable backbones
steps.focus: Compare point serialization with volumetric patch tokens and global attention.

steps.label: Separate object instances
steps.focus: Follow the change from point features to semantic, instance, and panoptic predictions.

steps.label: Transfer and generalize representations
steps.focus: Compare transferred 2D features with training across multiple 3D datasets.

routes.try_it: For a kitchen scan, sketch the difference between a semantic map, an instance map, and a panoptic map.

routes.title: 🗣️ Connect language, objects, and function
routes.summary: Open vocabulary → scene relations → actionable parts
routes.goal: Move from naming objects to locating the parts and relationships relevant to a task.

steps.label: Build a queryable 3D map
steps.focus: See how visual and language features support queries beyond a fixed label set.

steps.label: Ground queries in instances
steps.focus: Compare how 2D observations and 3D proposals produce object-level masks.

steps.label: Add language and relations
steps.focus: Contrast referring-expression localization with a scene graph for reasoning and planning.

steps.label: Identify functional regions
steps.focus: Relate task descriptions and affordances to actionable parts and part poses.

routes.try_it: Compare the regions needed for 'find the refrigerator' and 'open the refrigerator': object, door, handle, and action space.

routes.title: 🏗️ Reconstruct a whole 3D scene
routes.summary: Camera geometry → neural representations → learned geometry → online mapping
routes.goal: Compare ways to recover scene structure and appearance from images, depth, and video.

steps.label: Recover cameras and geometry
steps.focus: Compare image-based structure from motion with globally consistent RGB-D fusion.

steps.label: Represent scene appearance
steps.focus: Contrast a continuous radiance field with explicit Gaussian primitives; separate rendering quality from surface geometry.

steps.label: Predict geometry directly
steps.focus: Study feed-forward point maps, camera recovery, depth, and multi-view consistency.

steps.label: Map an ongoing observation stream
steps.focus: Compare implicit and Gaussian maps jointly updated with camera tracking.

steps.label: Handle a changing scene
steps.focus: Distinguish time-varying geometry and camera estimation from dynamic-scene rendering.

routes.try_it: For one captured room, list which methods need depth, camera poses, multiple views, or scene-specific optimization, and which outputs support rendering or geometry queries.

routes.title: 🌍 Generate scenes and environments
routes.summary: Layouts → visual scenes → procedural worlds → interactive simulation
routes.goal: Follow how scene generation combines room structure, object placement, appearance, and task requirements.

steps.label: Arrange objects in a scene
steps.focus: Compare autoregressive layout prediction with diffusion over scene configurations.

steps.label: Control composition with language
steps.focus: Study how text conditions become object relations and spatial layouts.

steps.label: Synthesize a visual 3D world
steps.focus: Contrast a generated textured room mesh with interactive scene expansion from an image.

steps.label: Generate environments procedurally
steps.focus: Compare interactive indoor-house sampling with procedural natural-world geometry and materials.

steps.label: Connect generation to embodied tasks
steps.focus: Read for task-driven scene construction and the interface between generated environments and agent training.

routes.try_it: Give the same room description to a layout generator, a visual scene generator, and a simulator-environment generator. List the different outputs and what each would still need for a robot task.

routes.title: ⚙️ Understand what moves, and how
routes.summary: Parts → joints and pose → tracking → scene articulation
routes.goal: Distinguish movable-part segmentation, motion parameters, articulated pose, and temporal tracking.

steps.label: Recover parts and motion
steps.focus: Compare motion-part analysis with category-level pose and canonical part coordinates.

steps.label: Track articulated state
steps.focus: Study how previous-frame estimates support online per-part pose tracking.

steps.label: Work from a single image
steps.focus: Follow openable-part detection and axis estimation from single-object to multi-object images.

steps.label: Scale to indoor scenes
steps.focus: Examine scene-level parts, handles, connectivity, and articulation predictions.

routes.try_it: For one door and one drawer, list the part mask, joint type, axis, origin, and state a robot would need.

routes.title: 🧩 Build an articulated digital twin
routes.summary: Observations → geometry and motion → executable models
routes.goal: Recover the geometry, joints, and executable structure of objects that move within a scene.

steps.label: Observe multiple states
steps.focus: Compare before/after interaction observations with multi-view capture in two states.

steps.label: Reconstruct from video
steps.focus: Study geometry, part decomposition, and articulation recovery from monocular video.

steps.label: Produce executable structure
steps.focus: Compare reconstructed parts and articulation code with single-image, mesh-based URDF prediction.

steps.label: Make static assets interactive
steps.focus: Inspect part detection, motion inference, hidden-geometry completion, and scene assembly.

routes.try_it: Make an input/output table: single image, two states, video, or static mesh in; geometry, joints, and executable assets out.

routes.title: 🛠️ Generate articulated assets
routes.summary: Part graphs → conditional generation → asset programs
routes.goal: Understand how geometry and kinematic structure are generated together under different conditions.

steps.label: Represent the articulation graph
steps.focus: Read for graph representations, part geometry, motion parameters, and structural constraints.

steps.label: Add physical or text conditions
steps.focus: Compare physical guidance and partial observations with text-conditioned tree generation.

steps.label: Generate from an image
steps.focus: Compare plausible geometry and kinematics inferred from one image.

steps.label: Author assets through programs
steps.focus: Trace how language/vision models produce programs defining parts, joints, and simulator assets.

routes.try_it: Compare two plausible models of the same closed cabinet: what can the image determine, and what must the generator infer?

routes.title: 🧭 Navigate with maps, language, and memory
routes.summary: Spatial maps → semantic goals → language instructions → lifelong navigation
routes.goal: Connect scene representations to where an agent should move and what it should remember.

steps.label: Build a language-queryable map
steps.focus: Follow visual-language feature fusion into a spatial map for navigation goals and obstacles.

steps.label: Explore toward a semantic goal
steps.focus: Study how frontier exploration and goal recognition guide object-goal navigation.

steps.label: Follow a language instruction
steps.focus: Trace landmarks from language through visual grounding to low-level navigation.

steps.label: Test instructions and memory
steps.focus: Compare route-following from natural language with repeated category, image, and language goals.

routes.try_it: For “find the mug near the sofa,” separate the target description, the map representation, the exploration decision, and memory carried over from earlier goals.

routes.title: 💡 Reason and answer questions about a 3D world
routes.summary: Gather observations → ground questions → reason → plan
routes.goal: Explore how an agent uses scene observations to answer questions and choose meaningful actions.

steps.label: Define the information-gathering task
steps.focus: Compare navigation to gather evidence with episodic-memory and active-exploration question answering.

steps.label: Give language models 3D context
steps.focus: Study the interface between 3D scene features and language-based questions, dialogue, and plans.

steps.label: Connect perception to multiple tasks
steps.focus: Compare 3D vision-language-action instruction tuning with continuous visual and robot-state inputs to language models.

steps.label: Ground an executable plan
steps.focus: Contrast high-level plans grounded through a controller with skill selection constrained by learned feasibility.

routes.try_it: Compare answering “what is on the kitchen table?” from remembered images with actively exploring to answer it. What evidence is missing, and which action would reveal it?

routes.title: 🦾 Turn perception into robot interaction
routes.summary: Affordances → motion planning → feedback → mobile manipulation
routes.goal: Follow the information a robot needs to choose a contact, move an articulated object, and adapt.

steps.label: Choose where to interact
steps.focus: Compare actionability predictions with affordances conditioned on occlusion and robot position.

steps.label: Represent the motion
steps.focus: Contrast dense motion fields with articulation models and adaptive joint estimation.

steps.label: Use history and contact
steps.focus: Study uncertain motion hypotheses from observation history and adaptation through tactile feedback.

steps.label: Bring the robot to the object
steps.focus: Connect perception to navigation, whole-body planning, grasping, and adaptation at real sites.

routes.try_it: Trace one failed door-opening attempt: what would a new camera view, contact measurement, or base movement change?

routes.title: 🤖 Connect generalist policies and embodied agents
routes.summary: Action learning → vision-language-action → planning and recovery
routes.goal: Compare learned action policies with language-guided planning and their interfaces to scene understanding.

steps.label: Learn action distributions
steps.focus: Read for conditional action diffusion, visual conditioning, and receding-horizon execution.

steps.label: Connect vision, language, and action
steps.focus: Study flow-matching action experts and co-training across robot and semantic data.

steps.label: Compare open policy foundations
steps.focus: Contrast a vision-language-action model with a transformer diffusion policy across embodiments and adaptation settings.

steps.label: Ground language plans
steps.focus: Compare affordance-value-guided skill selection with programs that build 3D value maps.

steps.label: Recover through interaction
steps.focus: Follow the link from semantic and actionable parts to executable policies and feedback after failure.

routes.try_it: For 'put the cup in the cabinet,' separate task planning, scene grounding, contact selection, and action execution.

routes.title: 📊 Choose data and evaluation for your task
routes.summary: Scene labels → functional annotations → simulation → household tasks
routes.goal: Match the desired capability to observations, annotations, environments, and evaluation protocols.

steps.label: Evaluate scene understanding
steps.focus: Compare high-fidelity scene capture with long-tail semantic and instance label coverage.

steps.label: Add function and articulation
steps.focus: Compare mobility annotations, task-grounded functional regions, and executable articulated scene structure.

steps.label: Use interactive object assets
steps.focus: Explore physics-based part interaction and procedural articulated-object data.

steps.label: Benchmark manipulation
steps.focus: Compare task coverage, robot interfaces, observations, demonstrations, and learning settings.

steps.label: Evaluate household activity
steps.focus: Study compositional kitchen-task generalization and long-horizon activity with dynamic object states.

steps.label: Evaluate reasoning and instruction following
steps.focus: Separate question-answering accuracy, household task completion, and dialogue-conditioned interaction.

routes.try_it: Choose one benchmark for scene segmentation and one for opening a cabinet; write down their inputs, success metrics, and generalization splits.
